messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER -> node-flap: usw2-infer-node-07 moved to NotReady x3 within 5m. Pod churn on inference-pool-usw2, observed container restarts and GPU driver errors. Pager: oncall (Sasha K).

Sasha K: Acknowledged. I'm on it. Marking priority P1 and pinging @Ravi P and @Marta L. Any immediate customer-facing alerts?

Ravi P: seeing the same. `kubectl get nodes | grep NotReady` shows 3 nodes flickering in us-west-2-a. Pods on inference pool are Restarting with exit code 137 + "CUDA unknown error" in logs for some replicas.

Marta L: copying metrics — latency spiked to 750ms p95 and error rate to ~4.2% on hosted route /v1/generate-usw2. Some customers showing increased 5xx. I'm flagging traffic to fallback routing.

Sasha K: quick plan: (1) throttle new requests to the affected pool, (2) divert to standby region / model variant, (3) isolate flaky nodes (cordon/taint) so scheduler won't place more pods, (4) collect kubelet logs & dmesg, (5) if nodes are OOMing or driver crashing, trigger infra escalation.

Ravi P: running diagnostics now. attaching outputs: 
```
# node status snapshot
NAME                 STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
usw2-infer-node-05   Ready      gpu      43d   v1.27.1
usw2-infer-node-07   NotReady   gpu      47d   v1.27.1
usw2-infer-node-11   NotReady   gpu      39d   v1.27.1
usw2-infer-node-14   NotReady   gpu      22d   v1.27.1
```
Logs from kubelet on node-07: 
```
Mar 12 10:04:12 kubelet[1234]: E03012 10:04:12 eviction-manager: eviction signal: memory.available below threshold
Mar 12 10:04:13 dockerd: containerd: runtime: failed to start container: failed to allocate cgroup resources
Mar 12 10:04:14 nvidia-driver: NVRM: GPU lockup
Mar 12 10:04:16 systemd: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=137
```

Ravi P: also seeing repeated `nvidia: failed to initialize NVML` in kernel logs -> possible driver crash.

Marta L: Customer impact estimate: ~8% of active requests hitting inference-pool-usw2 failing currently. Top affected tenants: customer-a, customer-b. Sending incident notice to SRE + CS.

Sasha K: Good. @DevOps Bot please cordon node-07/11/14 and kick a drain with --ignore-daemonsets for the most unstable ones. We don't want to cause extra churn if kubelet is unstable, but we need to stop scheduling.

DevOps Bot: `kubectl cordon usw2-infer-node-07 && kubectl drain usw2-infer-node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` queued. Will retry 3x if evict fails.

Ravi P: cordon succeeded for node-07. Drain partially succeeded; one pod (llm-serving) kept restarting during eviction. I exec'd into the kubelet logs and there's an OOM kill on the runtime shim while pulling large models.

Marta L: while nodes are contained, I'm flipping traffic routing to prefer eu-west-1 fallback pool and enabling fallback-model-lite on the hosted API for 10m to reduce p99 latency. Patch route: `/v1/generate -> prefer_region=eu-west-1, fallback_variant=lite`.

Sasha K: Approved. Marta, after flip, monitor client error rates and token throughput. If errors remain >2% for 5m escalate to infra.

Ravi P: digging deeper — kernel OOM might be triggered by host-level memory pressure plus GPU driver reinit attempts. I'm collecting `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200` and `dmesg`. Uploading to the incident S3.

Ravi P: snippet from dmesg: 
```
[  5122.334567] Out of memory: Killed process 27412 (llm-server) total-vm:2123456kB, anon-rss:1023456kB, file-rss:0kB, shmem-rss:0kB
[  5122.334912] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  5122.335210] nvidia: probe of 0000:af:00.0 failed with error -110
```

eng-sre-bot: Escalation note: attaching oncall list for infra-engineering. Paging infra leads.

Sasha K: @eng-sre-bot please add a request to provisioning to spin up 4 new standby nodes in eu-west-1 and mark them ready for spillover. We need capacity to absorb the diverted traffic for 30-60m.

eng-sre-bot: Request created: infra/3872 - spin up 4 g5-large-equivalent nodes in eu-west-1. ETA ~7m.

Marta L: eu-west capacity up in 6m, I've started traffic reroute. Early signs good: error rate dropping to 1.1% and latency back to ~220ms p95.

Sasha K: Nice. Next actions: (A) keep nodes cordoned; avoid rebooting until infra confirms driver stability, (B) run kubelet restart on Node-07 only if driver rebinds cleanly, (C) run `nvidia-smi` in maintenance window to validate driver.

Ravi P: agreed. I'll hold on a full cluster reboot. For root cause debug I'll provision a debug node and replicate workload to reproduce driver OOM. Uploading crash dump to /incidents/1766009999/dumps.tar.gz

Marta L: CS notified customers with degraded experience (DM and status page). Adding note to status: "Partial degradation in us-west-2 inference pool; routing to fallback region; investigating GPU driver instability."

Sasha K: After 15m of stable fallback routing and eu-west handling load, we'll start node-level triage: (1) pull driver and kernel versions, (2) check for recent kubelet upgrades, (3) check for VM-level memory ballooning from other tenants.

Ravi P: preliminary kernel + driver matches: kernel 5.15.0-77, nvidia-driver 525.85.05. No recent kubelet upgrade in 2 weeks. Suspect host memory pressure pattern causing OOM -> driver resets.

Marta L: monitoring continues. current customer impact ~0.5% failed requests after reroute. Keeping status page updated.

Sasha K: Good job team. If any of the nodes re-appear as NotReady again, escalate to infra and keep traffic diverted. I'll set a follow-up incident review for 48h to look at driver upgrade plan and improved cgroup limits to avoid OOM cascade. :thumbsup:

Ravi P: logging final notes, will attach steps to reproduce and trace for next-day postmortem.

DevOps Bot: drain completed for node-11 and node-14. node-07 remains in NotReady state; kubelet still restarting.

Marta L: I'll start a canary to shift 10% back to usw2 in 30m if metrics stay green.

oncall-bot: Incident channel update: incident-1766009999 opened | priority P1 | lead: Sasha K | status: mitigated -> partial (traffic diverted).

Sasha K: closing the pager for now, leaving the incident open for root cause analysis. Thanks all.
